plan.rationale: Acme scores 92, the highest in the book: weekly active seats are down 61.4% to 119 against a 308 baseline [acme-usage-1], $4,500 sits uncollected [acme-stripe-2], and the $1,500/mo subscription renews in 12 days [acme-stripe-1]. The trailing 8 weeks are stable for a month then fall off a cliff (297→241→186→142→119) [acme-usage-1], which points at a lockout rather than gradual disengagement — MAR-5, "SSO login loop on Okta", is unresolved in Backlog [acme-linear-2], alongside MAR-6 on export timeouts over 50k rows [acme-linear-1]. Two conflicts the operator should see: Acme is only $1,500/mo while Lumen Health carries $6,800/mo and renews sooner, in 9 days [lumen-stripe-1], on a milder -28.8% decline [lumen-usage-1]; and Vertex Financial has an open security escalation, MAR-7 "Data residency breach during EU failover" [vertex-linear-2], which may deserve independent escalation on severity even though its risk score is 49. Acme still wins on compounding, time-boxed signals — and it is a design-partner account [acme-linear-3] that has never been contacted.

payload.title: Acme Robotics save play — escalate MAR-5 SSO loop, recover $4,500, renewal in 12 days
payload.description:
Acme is at risk score 92 with renewal in 12 days. Work in this order:

1. ESCALATE MAR-5 ("SSO login loop on Okta") out of Backlog today. Confirm with engineering whether the loop affects all Okta tenants or Acme's config specifically, and get an ETA you can commit to in writing.
2. VERIFY the causal link. Seats were flat for four weeks (312/305/318/297) then dropped to 241/186/142/119. Pull auth error logs for Acme over that window to confirm the drop is failed logins and not seat deprovisioning. If it is deprovisioning, this is a very different conversation — report back before sending any commitment.
3. ESCALATE MAR-6 ("Exports timing out over 50k rows") as secondary. Confirm whether Acme's export volumes exceed 50k rows.
4. HOLD dunning on the $4,500 uncollected invoice until the SSO fix ships. Chasing payment while the product is unusable will lose the renewal. Confirm with billing that no automated collection email goes out this week.
5. BOOK the call with Priya Raghunathan (Head of Operations) and bring the auth engineer. This account has never been contacted — do not let the first touch be a payment chase.
6. PREP a renewal position before day 10: if the fix has not shipped, come with a specific credit or term concession rather than asking for a decision on a broken product.

actions.summary: Email the customer — "The Okta login loop on your account"

payload.subject: The Okta login loop on your account
payload.body:
Priya,

We have an open bug on our side — an SSO login loop on Okta — and your active seats have dropped from around 308 to 119 over the last four weeks. Those two facts look connected, and if they are, most of your team has been unable to sign in rather than choosing not to.

I am escalating that ticket today, along with a second one on exports timing out above 50k rows. Separately, a $4,500 invoice has not collected; I would rather sort that out after your team is working again, not before.

Can you take 20 minutes this week? Send me a time and I will bring the engineer who owns the auth fix.

Dana Whitfield
